membership_validation.method: exact three-field raw tuple membership only

assessments.basis: Classifier Context Rot varies benign transcript length while holding the dangerous action/task fixed and reports large recall degradation across three frontier monitor families, with benign false-positive controls and released code.
assessments.scope: Supports context-length sensitivity for the paper's Claude Code/MonitorBench constructions and tested Opus/GPT/Gemini monitors; not arbitrary production transcripts or all monitor architectures.

assessments.basis: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring reports a low-FPR degradation after unstructured human feedback and a positive control from selective escalation/strong-prior scaffolding, with public artifacts.
assessments.scope: One experienced-reviewer Claude 3.6 Sonnet SHADE-Arena aware-agent/aware-monitor case study at the paper's strict FPR operating point; not evidence that human oversight generally hurts.

assessments.basis: CodeMonitorBench reports 71,000 generated candidates, 43,677 public-test passers and 23,081 hidden-test failures among those passers; public-test-overfit pressure worsens weak-verifier performance in most cells with a stronger-model positive control.
assessments.scope: Strong evidence for the paper's three-domain CodeMonitorBench and M1 public-check boundary, not arbitrary production repositories or stronger hidden test regimes.

assessments.basis: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring evaluates aware attackers across multiple monitor-awareness levels and two environments; additional task awareness does not monotonically remove adversarial failures, with hierarchical-sequential scaffolding as a positive control.
assessments.scope: Empirical lower-bound evidence over the tested evasion strategies, monitors and SHADE/CUA environments; not a universal upper bound on monitoring or programmatic verification.

assessments.basis: The worker implements a Jeffreys beta-binomial mixture confidence-sequence utility grounded in time-uniform inference and identifies pseudoreplication in a public vLLM repeat-comparison case, but the role-local implementation was not independently exercised here.
assessments.scope: Valid only under the declared Bernoulli/filtration or appropriately modeled cluster contract; it does not repair arbitrary workload/server dependence or runtime drift.

assessments.basis: Peer-reviewed lemma-selection work scores candidate utility by counterfactual reproving under the base prover and reports downstream proof-subterm use plus transfer to other provers, directly measuring behavioral marginal effect rather than retrieval frequency.
assessments.scope: Condensed-detachment ATP experiments and per-problem selected lemmas only; not an optimal persistent global Lean/LLM library policy.

assessments.basis: The LEGO-Prover re-evaluation combines compute-matched baselines with behavioral audits and reports essentially no cross-task direct reuse despite hundreds of retrieved lemmas, with evidence against soft reuse.
assessments.scope: Isabelle/miniF2F LEGO-Prover only; does not show persistent theorem libraries are generally useless or rule out all guidance-only reuse.

assessments.basis: The IJCAR 2024 Vampire/QuickSpec study shows aggregate lemma gains while documenting per-problem lost proofs and increased proof time under otherwise comparable strategy families, directly showing non-monotonicity under bounded search.
assessments.scope: TIP induction benchmarks with QuickSpec/Vampire only; search-space explosion is plausible rather than a controlled single-factor ablation and this is not a persistent cross-task Lean-library test.

assessments.basis: Auto Research for Materials reports seven isolated searches with 701 evaluated changes, freezes selected code before a one-time untouched holdout and finds 9/10 selected interventions remain best tested; the released artifact adds retained trials, frozen winners, certification records, hashes and claim-verification scripts.
assessments.scope: Supports the reported materials-ML held-out decision-transfer protocol and artifact auditability; not an independent full rerun or proof of source/study/batch-disjoint validation or general autonomous-science improvement.

assessments.basis: Pinned public Meta^n source exposes concrete provenance boundaries: post-merge serialization can obscure pre-merge single-lineage identity, the ARC adapter separates hidden TEST labels from search-visible data, and the inspected public CLI advertises ARC while lacking the production branch wiring the adapter.
assessments.scope: Public repository/orchestrator provenance only; the exact pre-public paper-run ARC executable and tested artifact identity remain unavailable, and missing public CLI wiring does not show the reported ARC result is false.
